steps.text: Catherine? Catherine!

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: ...Clara? It's so early... did you need something?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: *sigh* You're always so busy. I was worried I wouldn't find you at home... and I wouldn't have, if I didn't come so early.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Not that busy. I'm retired. I'm just going out to buy food for the week.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: How about you? How's your mutual aid association going?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Well, that is what I came for...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Do you think you could... help me?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Can I come with you to the grocer? It won't take long.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Alright, come and help me pick a new detergent. The one I'm using right now leaves behind too much limescale.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: You're still using Old Hank's? They changed their formula. It's cheaper, but nowhere as effective as it used to be...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: We can talk about this once we're at the shop. What's this about the mutual aid association? What do you need me for?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Well... you know that we are all from single-parent families, and we help babysit each other's children.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: It started out as a bunch of people sharing their schedules, so that they could leave their kids with someone when they have long shifts or a night shift.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: That's how we've been getting by for all these years...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I know. It's been quite a few years. I'm amazed at how you've kept it going, and taking care of all those kids.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: *sigh* The mutual aid association helped a lot with John. I was just returning the favor...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: But... there are a lot more single-parent families after the war.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: The association has to take care of a lot more kids. Nobody's home could fit them all, if we still did things the old way.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Some houses don't even have enough chairs, never mind desks for them to do their homework.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: So we were thinking about pooling our resources to rent a bigger place.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Do you have enough money?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: *sigh* We have more people, after all. We can come up with a fair amount when everyone chips in a little...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: But... well... Ian and I were looking for a place together, but we... we had a fight.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: He hasn't showed up at the association for four days...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Just let it go, Ian... there's nothing we can do if he doesn't want to rent.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: We'll keep looking...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: That bloody jerk! It's just a cafeteria warehouse! I asked around and I know for a fact his factory's not operating. What kind of 'other uses' could he have?

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: We may not have signed a contract yet, but we already paid our deposit...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: How could he just go back on his word like that?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: He did give us our deposit back...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: That's what I'm angry about. He just threw the bag of money at you without so much as an apology. The way he looked down at us...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: He was the one who broke his word. No explanation, not even so much as a polite word.

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: He thinks we're people he can just walk over, doesn't he?

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: ...Do you think he's trying to drive up the price?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I don't think so. He would have said something if that was the case, wouldn't he?

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: I bet he wanted us to ask. Whoever asks first is at a disadvantage. That's how it is with bargaining.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: *sigh* You really wanted this place, didn't you?

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: Of course I did. After all, you...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: ...Never mind. What I mean is, it's the right size and location. It took us such a long time to find it, and to get a deal done...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: It's his place, and he gets to make the decisions... we have to accept that, Ian.

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: Why do you keep defending that guy? Aren't we supposed to be on the same side?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: O-Of course we are, but there's nothing we can do about it...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: What are two old folks like us supposed to do about it? If you keep whining, it'll just make me feel worse.

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: Alright, sorry, I didn't mean to upset you.

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: See you around.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: ...Ian hasn't shown up at the association since.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I... I shouldn't have said what I said. Ian was just standing up for me...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I'm just too meek... I didn't dare to speak up against the factory owner. All I did was sigh and lament. Of course he would be angry.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Ian sometimes looks hesitant when he's talking to me. Has he been tired of my attitude for a long time?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Why couldn't I be like you...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: ...You don't need to be like me, Clara. Lindy wouldn't have been so angry with me if I had half your gentleness.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: At least, she would have been happier. I think.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: See, there comes a time for everyone when they're not happy with themselves.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Catherine...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: But that's enough for that. So, do you want me to help you take care of this matter?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: No, I just...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Can you come with me to meet with the factory owner again... and have my back?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Ian was right. If he wanted to haggle, well, we can talk about it. At least he wouldn't demand an exorbitant price if he sees you...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Every factory owner in Highbury knows you, after all.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: If I can get the deal done, then I can apologize to Ian...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: How do you plan to pay for the extra expense?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I... I can pay it out of my own pocket, if it's not too much...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I-Is that alright? I hope I'm not troubling you too much...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Of course I'll help. And don't ever talk about troubling me. No need to treat me as a war hero. I'm just the same Catherine you've known for so long, the one who couldn't knit a sweater to save her life.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Let's see what's going on.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: What are you doing here? I gave you back your deposit. I don't owe you a pence now.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: What... what if we're willing to pay more for the rent?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Do you think you could, er, think about it...

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Do I look like I'm after that little bit of rent you're paying?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Wh-What's your price? We can talk about it...

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Are you deaf, grandma?

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: If I'm not renting, I'm not renting. I'm being nice because of your age. You should be grateful.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: You call that being nice?

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: What's that, another grandm—wait, y-you're that war hero?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I'm Catherine Fletcher.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: ...Fine. What do you want?

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: I'm not planning to reopen the factory. No workers for you to rally. There's nothing you can do to me.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Besides, this is my property, and I get to decide what to do with it. I didn't even sign a contract with her. She's not a tenant, and there's no law that can do anything about it.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: I'm showing plenty of good faith by giving her back the deposit.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: First, explain what you mean when you say you're not planning to reopen the factory.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Oh, where's this going? That 'social responsibility' stuff?

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Me and my rotten luck. No good deed ever goes unpunished in this city.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Sounds like you have a lot on your hands. Maybe we can find some common ground, in which case I might be able to help.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: ...Why do you want to help me?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Why shouldn't I, if helping you helps the workers?

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Alright, at least you're not one of those bucket-heads who only know how to yell.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: But don't bother.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: You want to talk social responsibility, come back later and talk to the Columbians.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: You sold the factory to the Columbians?

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Not the whole factory, just the buildings. The factory is bankrupt.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Just because we won the war doesn't mean people like me got access to any loans.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: If you can sell the buildings, you can put it up for collateral. I know a thing or two about these things.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: No, you don't. If the Columbians didn't buy my buildings, they would buy somebody else's. At the prices they set, I wouldn't even be able to pay the interest if I tried to compete with them.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: I hung in there for two years... I was happy when we won the war. I thought I had made it.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: I could have hung on for a few more months... or so I thought. But then the Columbians came, and I didn't need to anymore.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Unless you thought I could hire workers at half-wage, 'leader of the workers'?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: No. Parliament wouldn't allow it.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Thanks to that Minimum Wage Bill that you people passed in Parliament...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: For you, going bankrupt means selling your factory for a nice little sum that would let you live comfortably in retirement at your country manor.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Do you know what it means for the workers if their wages get slashed in half?

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: I do, whether you believe it or not.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: I failed because I knew these things.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Or you were just unlucky.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: The workers need not, and cannot, take responsibility for your bad luck.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: ...I hate talking to people like you.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I don't hate talking to you. You're hardly the worst person I've met.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I hope luck will favor the people of this city.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I asked Clara what price you set. Like you said, you didn't rent her the warehouse for the money.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: ...It's not like I didn't want to do some good. If heaven would let me.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: But heaven didn't show as much kindness to me as I tried to show others.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Bah, forget it. Why am I even telling you this.

steps.name: Factory Owner
steps.text: Anyway, the warehouse's sold. You heard me? Don't come back.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: 'It's not that I don't want to help, I just can't help anymore.' Is that what you think?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: If that's really the case, maybe you can hear me out. There's still a way for you to gain some appreciation, if you're up for it.
A few days later...

steps.name: Tall Worker
steps.text: I'm done over here, Catherine!

steps.name: Short-sighted Worker
steps.text: What? No way you worked faster than me—

steps.name: Tall Worker
steps.text: You bet I did! I want my pint of beer.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Good work, folks. Drinks are on me.

steps.name: Tall Worker
steps.text: No! We had a bet. He owes me one, even if you're buying.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: This round's still on me. You can collect from him later.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Please, allow me. Come over to my place afterwards, Bernie, Galvin and Catherine, and let me play host.

steps.name: Tall Worker
steps.text: No need to be so polite, Clara. It's just a little prefab, easily done.

steps.name: Short-sighted Worker
steps.text: Yeah, spend that money on food for the kids, not beer for Bernie.

steps.name: Tall Worker
steps.text: I'll let you settle that bet by turning the beer you owe me to bread for Clara.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: But you've helped so much...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: They're on the night shift today, Clara. They can't come.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Oh... alright. Another day, then.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: What about you, Catherine? You have the time, don't you? This could never have happened without you...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I couldn't have imagined that the factory owner was a good man... I hardly dared breathe when the two of you were talking the other day.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Good man, huh... I suppose.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: You won't find an empty plot of land in Highbury, outside of scattered spaces on factory premises. Fortunately, all he sold were the buildings, not the land.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Will we be alright when the Columbians come?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: No problem. I had a look at the place that day. There wasn't much use for this little corner anyway, other than storing some junk.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: We'll patch up that brick wall later so that it'll be separated from the factory area.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Besides, we have a proper lease signed this time. Today's Londinium has some rules, at least. There's nothing to be afraid of.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: It's all thanks to you, Catherine...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: All I've done is help out for a couple of days. It's nothing compared to how you've been taking care of the kids for so long.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: It's not like I'm good for much else at my age... it's not so much that I'm taking care of the kids as the kids are keeping me company.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Oh dear, look at me, being pessimistic again. You're not offended, are you?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: No, I'm not. I know that's the kind of person you are. Whatever you think about yourself, Clara, I think you're amazing.
To Catherine's surprise, Clara looks sad at the answer, as though it brought back unpleasant memories.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Are you thinking about Ian? Unhappy that he's cross with you?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: ...Maybe. I can tell that sometimes when he looked at me, there's something he wanted to say, but couldn't say out loud.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: If you can tell what he's thinking, he can tell what you're thinking. Perhaps he has his own considerations.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: That day... I was quite sure there was something he wanted to say to me, but he never actually said it. Then he just got angry with me for days. What was I supposed to do...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I know, I shouldn't have said that he made me feel worse...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I want to invite everyone from the association to gather once I've cleaned up the place... do you think Ian will come?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Don't ask me. Ask him.
Day of the gathering

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Can I plant something here, Clara? My teacher wants us to observe how seeds sprout. I brought the peas and cans!

steps.name: Composed Child
steps.text: Don't tell me you're trying to make canned peas sprout.

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Don't be silly! I'm not stupid. My dad bought fresh peas from the grocery store!

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Can I plant them, Clara? Can I?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Of course, darling. There's some dirt piled up over there that you can use.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Do you take care of all these children by yourself?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: There aren't so many usually. They came because of the gathering...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I'm not by myself. The others take turns to come over and help. I don't have to go to work, so I have more time.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Ian's retired too. He can help you.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Is he not here?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: ...I went to his place a couple of days ago to tell him about the gathering, but he wasn't at home.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I left a message with his neighbor, but...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Is he avoiding me?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: ...Have you ever thought about talking to him, Clara?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Talk... about what?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Forming a family, the two of you.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Wh-What are you talking about?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I'm not saying you have to form a family, but at least let him know that you like him. Don't keep everything in your heart.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: C-Catherine, I... I... you...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Did you think I couldn't tell?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: But... at my age...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: What good is there in hiding it? What do you have to lose by saying it?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: But people don't talk about these things at this age...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: What about 'this age'? It's not like your brain's stop working, or your heart's stop beating. You like being with him, care about him, and look all sullen when you don't see him. It's obvious, isn't it?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: People will gossip so much...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: And what about it? All the things that you and Ian have done at the association, what kind of person you are, it's there for everyone to see.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Taking care of children is a good thing. This is different. It's so... shameful...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I, I don't mean to say you're wrong, Catherine. I'm just... I'm talking about myself...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Are you saying that you're being 'shameful'?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I know you. You always treat people sincerely, as you treat Ian.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: There's nothing shameful about being sincere.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I know we're at 'this age', but all the more reason to go for what you want, while you can.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: How much time do we have left? What is there to worry about?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: But... he's still angry with me... what do I do...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: You know what kind of man Ian is, don't you? Kind, gentle soul, just like you. Did you really think he would stay angry with you?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Even if it's not today...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Oh, look who's here.

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: *huff*... *huff*...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Ian!

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: You... you came?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Why are you in such a hurry...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: Baldi didn't tell me until this morning! He was grinning from ear to ear, saying, 'I almost forgot! Clara came to look for you again...'

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: That bloody bastard!

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I thought you were angry with me...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: I... yes, I was a little angry that day.

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: I... never mind.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Don't 'never mind'. Clara gets anxious when you swallow your words like that, like she's been these few days.

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: I... I wanted to have the association here because... because Clara is the one who cares for the children the most.

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: The other places were all too far from her home...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: How much time would it take for her to go back and forth with her bad legs? What if she has an accident?

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: I... I was concerned for her, only to be told that I was being upsetting...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: I was a little hurt.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Oh... Ian...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: I'm so sorry, Ian! You know I always say the wrong things... I didn't really mean it...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: I know. I stopped being angry the next day.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Then why didn't you come to the association?

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: ...I was out all day these few days, trying to come up with the money and see if I could negotiate with the factory owner...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: Then I learned from Baldi this morning that you and Catherine had taken care of it!

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: He didn't dare play games when he saw Catherine, did he?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Depends on how you define 'playing games'.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: By the way, I think Clara has something to say to you.

steps.name: Clara & Ian
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: Clara...?
Clara subconsciously clutches the edge of her jacket.
In that moment, it is as though the clock has been turned back forty years.
That day, Clara had clutched the edge of her white skirt in the same way, stuttering as she said the three magical words.
There are wrinkles all over her face now, but the expression upon it is no different from the young girl in the white dress forty years ago.
Clara opens her mouth, but no words come out.
It feels as though the air has become dense... then she hears Clara's voice.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: ...Ian.

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Catherine said to me... no, Catherine didn't put me to this. I wanted to say it myself...

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: Ian... what do you say that we... got together?

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: We... what?

steps.name: Clara
steps.text: See, you've helped me so much, and I think... I think you're really nice. What do you think about me... about you and me?

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: Clara... good heavens...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: How... how could I have made you say it... I've always... I know that you... you would have minded...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: I... heavens, Clara, I never thought... never thought you would...

steps.name: Ian
steps.text: O-Of course! I think you're really fine, really!
They say no more, their hands holding each other's tightly.
Catherine turns her head in the direction of the racket that the children are making.
The sky is overcast, but it seems to have gotten brighter than when it was an hour ago.
But of course, it is morning.
And the sun is rising.
